errors.quote: a competitive inhibitor raising Km,app from 20 → 60 µM and an uncompetitive inhibitor cutting Vmax to ~52 nmol/min (with corresponding Km reduction) can produce indistinguishable single-point rates.
errors.issue: The first rate is 900/70=12.857 nmol/min. Preserving Km/Vmax for the second gives Km=11.556 and v=24.124 nmol/min. These are distinguishable examples; an uncompetitive Vmax near 18 is needed for the first rate.

errors.quote: Single substrate, single active site, no cooperativity
errors.issue: A hyperbolic kinetic law does not establish that an enzyme has only one active site.

errors.quote: the hyperbolic equation fails and the Morrison quadratic form is needed.
errors.issue: This is too categorical: substantial substrate sequestration requires an appropriate mass-balance/kinetic treatment; a named tight-binding inhibitor formula is not automatically required in this inhibitor-free packet.

rationale: Correct headline answer but consequential errors in the worked mechanism example and unjustified model restrictions. The elaborate protocol does not repair those logical faults.
